correctness.rationale: The claims are correct for the standard model in characteristic >=11. The Jacobian of the power sums has full rank on the curve; the canonical quadric is nondegenerate on the sum-zero hyperplane. The asserted tangent identities, coordinate polynomials, and discriminants were independently checked. A potential root-ratio collision would force F(-2)=-2 or F(-3/2)=5/8 to vanish; the second-plane coefficients are nonzero, pairwise distinct, and sum to -20. Distinct supports are distinguished modulo adding a constant vector: when there is no common zero coordinate, a putative affine equivalence forces two unequal supported coefficients to agree. The non-stall coordinates have no projective scaling ambiguity since their quintic has nonzero linear and constant coefficients, forcing c^4=c^5=1. The tangent-plane evaluation criterion and degree 6 then give exactly the specified contacts. To fill out two standard premises: the transposition of repeated stall coordinates sends a uniformizer to its negative, and every tangent plane is invariant. The two-dimensional vector space of tangent planes has a nonzero combination cancelling the quadratic term, hence contact order >=4. The canonical Wronskian has degree 60 and is nonzero because distinct vanishing orders at a point are bounded by 6 < p, so these are all the stalls. On the smooth canonical quadric a degree-three pencil is cut out by a ruling (its divisors span lines by Riemann–Roch); the ruling bundles are distinct on the (3,3) curve, for H^0(O_C(1,-1))=0 by the quadric restriction sequence. Thus no effective even theta gives additional tritangents. Root-label permutations have trivial stabilizers in every displayed configuration, giving exactly d,d,lcm(d,e) and the stated counts and Euler products.
residual_risks: Neither the check nor the theorem treats twists or characteristics below 11, nor the zeta function of the underlying curve.
